thread.title: AMD: Poised To Repeat In 2019 - Advanced Micro Devices, Inc. (NASDAQ:AMD)

author: Stone Fox Capital
title: AMD: Poised To Repeat In 2019 - Advanced Micro Devices, Inc. (NASDAQ:AMD)
text:
One of my favorite picks in 2018 faltered to end the year. By all accounts, Advanced Micro Devices ( AMD ) had a huge year, but some in the market view the year as a failure with questioned prospects going forward. The reality is that a secular shift presents AMD with the ability to repeat the biggest gain in the S&P 500 index again in 2019.
Image Source: AMD January 2019 presentation
Top Gainer In 2018 AMD just completed a year where the stock ended up nearly 80% and the company l ed the S&P 500 in gains for the year. The natural mindset is that AMD can't repeat those gains in 2019.
The mindset would be flawed as stocks usually have multi-year runs when secular shifts take place. All one needs to do is look at fellow chip stock Nvidia ( NVDA ). The stock led the S&P 500 index with a 227% gain in 2016. Only one other stock had a gain in excess of 100% that year.
Source: Motley Fool
Nvidia followed that up with another 81% gain in 2017. AMD almost lost 10% that year.
NVDA data by YCharts
Noteworthy is that Nvidia saw gains in both years that exceeded what AMD accomplished in 2018. This clear example shows that a multi-year run is possible here, especially when the stock had a losing year in 2017.
Maybe most important for a strong 2019 return is that AMD gave up huge gains at the end of 2018. The stock reached a high of $34.14 back in September and a return to that high in 2019 would involve an 85% gain from the $18.46 starting price for the year.
Epyc Shift A lot of people selling the stock to end 2018 are too focused on the current semiconductor cycle and not fully embracing the shift in the datacenter space. AMD is poised to grab significantly market share in the sector. The Epyc chip delivers better performance at every price point so it's only a matter of time before the company reaches the predicted 2019 double-digit market share and my own projections of returning to 20% levels.
Source: AMD January 2019 presentation
The total market opportunity in the datacenter space is targeted at $29 billion in 2021. The CPU segment is $17 billion and AMD expects to continue taking share in this segment due to deals with cloud service providers like AWS, Microsoft Azure and Oracle Cloud and the Chinese offerings from Baidu and Tencent.
Source: AMD January 2019 presentation
Boosting Targets A disappointing rehash in the January 2019 presentation is the slide on the long term financial models. The company should finally be ready to update a model that doesn't accurately reflect the current market opportunity, especially with higher margin products.
AMD has provided these long-term financial targets:
Revenue - double-digit growth Gross Margin - ~40% - 44% Opex - ~26% - 30% EPS - >$0.75 The key to this target missed by the market is that AMD forecast an EPS in excess of $0.75. The market has always focused on the company maxing out at that level and it doesn't help that 2019 estimates are currently at only $0.62.
The question really isn't how AMD exceeds those targets, but how quickly and how far above the company can reach. Analysts have meager revenue growth estimates for 2019 and the weak Apple ( AAPL ) numbers after the close on Wednesday aren't going to help.
AMD is exiting 2018 with GPU inventory issues that recently crushed Nvidia. The cryptocurrency bust ended last Q1 with about $125 million in quarterly revenues so that headwind actually becomes a tailwind as the year transpires.
The question has to be how AMD doesn't gain market share in CPUs, especially in datacenter. To reach the double-digit 2019 goal for servers, AMD would have to capture about $1.3 billion in additional sales from 2018 levels. Analysts are only forecasting 2019 sales growth of about $480 million.
AMD Revenue Estimates for Current Fiscal Year data by YCharts
The analyst estimates ( per Benzinga ) before this market selloff were for server CPU sales of $324 million in 2018 and $824 million this year. At a market size of $13 billion in 2019, at least 10% market share is an incredible $1.0 billion boost to sales alone that the market doesn't appear to be accurately forecasting.
Analyst estimates continue to be far too low for the next couple of years. For AMD to reclaim 20% market share similar to server market share back in 2006, revenue estimates for CPU server sales alone would reach $3.4 billion by 2021. The company would see a $3.0 billion boost to the $6.5 billion revenue estimate for 2018.
Source: Marketwatch
This number has no gains for PCs or datacenter GPUs or even machine learning that will reach a market size of $12 billion. For this reason, my estimates suggests these long-term targets that AMD is likely to update the market this year:
Revenue - double-digit growth Gross Margin - ~44% - 48% Opex - ~24% - 28% EPS - > $1.25 The company is likely to provide these targets for 2021/2022, but a couple of key points could push the realization to 2020. Naturally, the market share gains in server CPU sales due to Epyc 2 are a key component. The other fact is all of the new chips already generate gross margins in excess of 50%.
The only real issue are the revenue levels as global economic weakness could make current analyst estimates more likely. The current 2019 forecasted revenue growth at 6% just doesn't appear plausible with the market share gains. For this reason, my targets for 2020 are as follows:
Revenue - $10+ billion Gross Margin - 48% Opex - 24% EPS - >$1.50 With revenues up 50% in that period, AMD should be able to push operating expenses down to 24%. Combined with a big boost in 50%+ gross margin products like Ryzen, Radeon and Epyc, the company should see a large boost to operating margins. A few percentage points in both directions is what will push their historically low margins to more normal levels in the sector.
Takeaway The key investor takeaway is that history shows that a company in the market share gain phase can easily generate multi-year runs. At $18, AMD is likely to see substantial upside when the company updates their financial models to higher EPS estimates going forward.
The weak Apple guidance is likely to roil the sector for the rest of the week, but AMD remains a stock to buy on weakness with reasonable EPS targets in excess of $1.50 and approaching levels of 12x that estimate. With those numbers, the stock is poised to repeat the market-leading gains from 2018.
